prompt:
Create ONE landscape animal reference sheet showing the SAME individual
cream Persian cat in exactly SIX full-body views, arranged as THREE COLUMNS
and TWO ROWS with clear whitespace and no printed labels or divider lines.
Read the layout left to right:
TOP ROW: standing FRONT; standing LEFT THREE-QUARTER; standing TRUE LEFT PROFILE.
BOTTOM ROW: standing BACK; SITTING LEFT THREE-QUARTER; LYING LEFT THREE-QUARTER.
One cat repeated six times as reference views, not six different individuals.
Do not add any other animal, human, accessory or inset.

REFERENCE IMAGE 1 is the cat identity source. Preserve this cream Persian's
natural adult proportions and distinctive rounded, full silhouette beneath
the long thick fur, abundant neck/chest ruff, round face with the short/flat
muzzle as it actually appears, visible ears, whiskers and fluffy tail/body
fur. Keep the creamy coat without adding tabby stripes, new patches or bright
white recolouring. Retain the source face rather than exaggerating a new
extremely flattened nose or breed hypertype. Keep the eyes' appearance
consistent with the source without a newly specified precise colour. Do not
invent a name, sex, exact measurements, collar or jewellery. Ignore the sofa,
blanket, room and warm lighting of image 1; they are not parts of the animal.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 is a GRAPHIC STYLE reference ONLY, the approved illustrated
adult portrait. Borrow its fine visible dark contours, painterly cel shadow
facets, restrained surface detail and realistic-proportion semi-anime language.
DO NOT depict the man, his face, hair, body, suit or room, and do not make the
cat human-faced or anthropomorphic. Harmonize gently toward this drawn style:
simplify individual fur strokes into readable locks and group shadows while
preserving the Persian's full neck ruff, thick long coat, silhouette, face and
natural feline anatomy from image 1. Not a photograph, plastic 3D render,
chibi, oversized-eyed mascot or fantasy cat. Do not replace this Persian with
a short-haired cat or change it into the tabby.

In the standing front view face the viewer on four naturally placed paws.
In the left three-quarter views show the anatomical left side and turn the nose
toward image-left. The TRUE LEFT PROFILE must show the ENTIRE body side-on:
head, shoulders, ribcage, pelvis, legs and paws all lateral, nose toward image-left;
not just a sideways head on a three-quarter chest. In BACK face away naturally.
SITTING is an ordinary resting seated cat with natural hindquarters and front
paws; LYING is a relaxed cat resting on its underside with the paws placed
naturally, consistent with the source's ordinary resting presence. Four correct
legs/paws per cat, allowing natural far-limb/fur occlusion, not extra or fused
limbs, and never standing on human-like hind legs. Keep the paws readable
where naturally visible without removing the approved full coat volume.

Keep the SAME body scale and proportions across all six views: seated and
lying poses naturally have different extents, do not enlarge them to fill
their cells. Include complete ears, whiskers, full fur silhouette, visible paws
and fluffy tail within each cell with comfortable margins. No clipped fur,
cut-off tails, overlapping views, distorted body length or duplicated paws.
New hidden anatomy and fur on unseen sides should be restrained plausible
completions of this same cat, not changes to its identity or coat.

Plain neutral-grey comparison background, soft diffuse even illumination
consistent across the sheet, restrained small grounding shadows and readable
cream fur volumes. Keep a subtle muted olive/charcoal painted-shadow sensibility
without staining the coat green or yellow. No amber nocturnal rim light,
dramatic black shadows, living-room scene, furniture, props, floor plan, text,
names, labels, panel borders, layout lines or watermark.
